title: Inhibition of Liver Fibrosis by Polygonatum sibiricum Based on Network Pharmacology Investigation
content: Background: Liver fibrosis (LF) is a chronic pathological process caused by hepatic pathological factors. Currently, there is no effective clinical method against LF. Polygonatum sibiricum (PS) is a commonly used traditional Chinese medicine. Studies have shown that PS can protect the liver and lower blood glucose and blood lipids. However, there are no clinically recognized drugs for the treatment of liver fibrosis. Research methods: This study utilized pharmacological networks and in vivo and in vitro experiments to investigate the mechanism of action of PS in improving LF. The mechanism and pathway of action of PS to improve LF were explored by CCK-8, Western blot, and immunofluorescence. The LF model was constructed by intraperitoneal injection of CCl4 (0.6 mL/kg) into C57BL/6 mice. The mice were given PS treatment by gavage. After four weeks, pathological changes in the liver were assessed by HE, Masson, and Sirius red staining. The expression of LF-related proteins in liver tissues was evaluated by immunohistochemistry (No. Cheng Medical Activity Lun [2024] 032). Results: PS inhibited α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), collagen type I α1 chain (COL1A1) and Bcl-2, promoted the expression of Bax and p53 signaling pathways and facilitated apoptosis in LX-2 cells. In in vivo experiments, PS reduced the serum levels of AST/ALT, inhibited the development of LF and decreased the expression of α-SMA, COL1A1 and COL3A1 in liver tissues. Conclusion: PS inhibits LX-2 proliferation and LF-associated protein expression by regulating the p53 signaling pathway, thereby improving LF.
